fields.meta_title: Pet Quiz: Which Pet Fits You? Build Your Own | Emergent
fields.meta_description: Take a pet quiz that matches your home and week to a dog, cat, rabbit, fish, or bird. Then build your own for an animal shelter or store.
fields.h1: Build a Pet Quiz That Matches People to the Right Pet
fields.hero_description: Get your match from the eight-question pet quiz below, then build one that saves each result to a database you own.
fields.features_heading: What Emergent Puts Inside a Pet Quiz
fields.features_subheading: One prompt builds the questions, the five results, and the table that stores them. Ask for a change, and Emergent makes it.
fields.feature_1:
Each answer counts toward one pet

Tell Emergent which pets your quiz can recommend and what each one needs from a home. It writes the questions, scores every option toward one pet, and rewrites any of it on request.
fields.feature_2:
Answers saved beside the result

Every finished quiz becomes a row in a database you own: the pet it named, each answer given, and the date. Sort a season of rows by pet, or open one row before an adopter visits.
fields.feature_3:
An email the moment a quiz is done

The app can email a shelter counselor or a shop owner when someone finishes, with the result and the answers in the message. Slack and in-app alerts work too if your team uses them.
fields.feature_4:
Made for a thumb, one question at a time

Visitors answer one question per screen, which suits a phone held in a shelter lobby or a store aisle. There is no cap on responses, so a busy adoption weekend never hits a limit.
fields.feature_5:
Results sent to the tools you already use

The app connects to any tool with an API, so an email left on the result screen can land in your newsletter tool or CRM. Data syncs both ways, and your database stays the record.
fields.feature_6:
Your domain, and your code on GitHub

Host the quiz on your shelter's or shop's own domain, which is included in Emergent and uses credits. On paid plans, export the full code to your GitHub repository and keep it.

fields.usecase_heading: Four Pet Quizzes and What Happens After
fields.tab_content_1:
Before Saturday, Ismay's answers reach her counselor

Ismay Coldwell takes the pet quiz on Marrowbrook Animal Shelter's site while booking a Saturday visit, and her result is Cat. Counselor Bautista Ruiz-Tagle gets an email with the result and her answers: alone 9 hours on weekdays, a lease that allows cats, and no kids at home. He has 2 adult cats ready to meet her at 2 pm.
fields.tab_content_2:
From 2,400 results, a small-animal aisle

Gillyflower Pet Supply put the pet quiz on its site and on a tablet by the register. From September through November, 2,400 people finished it, and the dashboard counts every result by pet. Rabbit results reached 480, more than fish and birds together. Owner Dorotea Zeller is giving rabbits their own aisle in the spring.
fields.tab_content_3:
Of 24 third graders, 14 missed the feeding question

Clemency Ebo wanted her class ready before a goldfish joined Room 12 at Ramsdell Elementary. She built a pet care quiz of 8 questions, and all 24 third graders took it on the class tablets. The results table showed that 14 of 24 missed question 5, on how often to feed a goldfish. She taught that part again on Friday.
fields.tab_content_4:
After the result, 413 readers asked for a guide

Petronella Maudsley writes Burrow and Perch, a blog about small pets and birds. Her pet quiz ends with a care guide for the matched pet, sent to readers who leave an email. In October, 413 of the 1,180 readers who finished left one. The app saves each email with its result and sends it to her newsletter tool through its API.

fields.howto_title: How to Write a Pet Quiz People Finish
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to write a pet quiz that matches people to a pet they can care for, then build it with Emergent.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 Name the pets you can recommend
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Map every option to one pet
fields.howto_step_1_des: Name the pets you can stand behind before you write a single question. Five works well: a dog, a cat, a rabbit, a fish, and a bird cover the homes a shelter or shop sees. Give each one a short note on the home and time it needs.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Write one question per part of daily life: hours at home, space, budget, noise, who else lives there, and how hands-on someone wants to be. Ask about the week as it is now, not the week people hope to have after the pet arrives.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Point every option at exactly one pet, and check that each pet appears in at least two questions. Read the options aloud. Four answers of the same kind and length keep people from steering toward the result they already want.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Eight questions are enough to separate five pets, and a quiz that size fits a coffee break or a wait at the register. Cut any question whose options all point to the same pet, since it adds a screen without changing anyone's result.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Write each result as where the answers lean, then add the first thing to plan for, such as a quiet room for a cat or floor space for a rabbit's pen. Present it as a starting point for a conversation with the shelter or shop.
fields.howto_step_6_des: Choose the next step before you build. A counselor email, a count by pet on a dashboard, or a care guide offered for an email each needs different fields saved. Put that next step in your prompt, and Emergent builds it with the quiz.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Test it on five real households
fields.howto_step_7_des: Before launch, ask five people with different homes to take the quiz and tell you whether their result surprised them. If two land on a pet that clearly misfits their week, rewrite the question that tipped them, then test again.

faq_plan.a: A pet quiz is a short set of questions about someone's home and schedule that recommends the kind of pet that fits, such as a cat or a rabbit. A shelter or a pet shop can run one to start a conversation about adoption or care.

faq_plan.q: How do I create a pet quiz?
faq_plan.a: Pick the pets your quiz can recommend, write 6 to 10 questions about daily life, and map each option to one pet. Then describe that quiz in Emergent's AI survey builder, and it builds the questions, the result screens, and the database that saves every result. A follow-up prompt adds an email alert or a dashboard.

faq_plan.q: What pet quiz questions should I ask to match someone with a pet?
faq_plan.a: Ask about the parts of a week that decide whether a pet fits: hours away from home, space, monthly budget, tolerance for noise, and how much daily care someone wants to give. Add one question on what they hope to do together, like long walks on weekends.

faq_plan.q: How many questions should a pet quiz have?
faq_plan.a: Aim for 8. That gives each of five pets room to appear in at least two questions and keeps the quiz short enough to finish on a phone. The quiz on this page uses 8 questions and 5 results, one for each pet.

faq_plan.q: How does a pet quiz decide which pet to recommend?
faq_plan.a: Each option adds a point to one pet, and the pet with the most points after the last question becomes the result. Set a tie rule too, such as the pet listed first. Emergent builds the scoring from your prompt, and a follow-up prompt changes it.

faq_plan.q: Can a pet quiz show adoptable animals that match the result?
faq_plan.a: Yes, when the quiz can read your adoption list. Tag each animal with the pet type the quiz returns, and the result screen lists the animals with that tag. Keep the list current, because an animal adopted last week should not appear as a match.

faq_plan.q: Should a pet quiz for kids be different from one for adults?
faq_plan.a: Yes. For kids, use shorter questions and plain options, with results built around care tasks they can help with, like feeding a fish. Leave the budget and lease questions for the adult version, and let a parent see the result before anyone visits a shelter.

faq_plan.q: What should happen after someone finishes a pet quiz?
faq_plan.a: Give the result one clear next step: book a shelter visit, read a care guide, or see the supplies a first-time owner needs. Keep the answers with the result as well. The person who follows up needs to know why the quiz chose a cat over a rabbit.

faq_plan.q: How can I track which pets my pet quiz recommends most?
faq_plan.a: Count results by pet on a dashboard and compare one season with the next. A rising pet tells a shop what to stock and a shelter which adopters to expect. An app built on Emergent has no response caps, and a busy month is counted in full.

faq_plan.q: Can I collect email addresses with a pet quiz?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Put an optional email field on the result screen and offer something tied to the result, like a care guide for that pet. Ask after the result, not before the first question. People who only wanted their answer will still finish.

quiz.title: Which Pet Fits Your Life?
quiz.intro: Eight questions about your home, your week, and the kind of company you want. Your result names the pet your answers lean toward and what to plan for first.

questions.text: How many hours is your home empty on a typical weekday?

options.text: Almost never, someone is home most of the day
8 hours or more, but my evenings are free
A few hours, and I'm home most evenings
Long days, and I travel some weekends
Someone is home most mornings and evenings

questions.text: What does your home look like?

options.text: An apartment with a sunny windowsill
A spare corner with room for a pen
A small studio with one free shelf
A bright room where a cage can sit near people
A house with a yard or a park nearby

questions.text: How do you picture a perfect Saturday with your pet?

options.text: Sitting on the floor while it explores
Watching it glide around while I unwind
Listening to it chatter while I cook
A long hike or a game of fetch
Reading while someone naps on my lap

questions.text: How much hands-on care do you want to give each day?

options.text: A few minutes of feeding and a weekly tank check
Daily chats, fresh food, and a cage to tidy
An hour or more of walks, play, and training
Some play, then a litter box to scoop
Fresh hay and time out of the pen

questions.text: How do you feel about noise at home?

options.text: Singing and chirping all morning sounds great
Barking at the door is fine with me
I like a quiet home with the odd meow
Near silence, apart from a thump now and then
Only the hum of a filter
Kids who want a playmate for the yard
Just me, or one other calm adult
Older kids who can sit quietly on the floor
Roommates who are rarely around
A partner who works from home

questions.text: What kind of bond are you hoping for?

options.text: An independent friend who chooses when to cuddle
A gentle companion that learns to trust me
A calm, living centerpiece for my room
A chatty companion with opinions
A shadow who follows me everywhere

questions.text: How much space can you give up for supplies?

options.text: Room for a pen, a hay bin, and a hideaway
A sturdy stand for a tank
A tall cage and a perch by the window
A crate, a leash hook, and a bin of toys
A litter box corner and a scratching post

results.title: Your Match: A Dog
results.description: Your answers lean toward an active pet that wants to be with you most of the day. Plan for daily walks and play, a few training sessions, and a sitter or walker for long workdays. A shelter counselor can help you narrow it down by size and energy.

results.title: Your Match: A Cat
results.description: Your answers lean toward a quieter home and a pet that is content on its own for part of the day. Plan for a litter box spot, a scratching post, and some play each evening. Ask a shelter about adult cats as well as kittens.

results.title: Your Match: A Rabbit
results.description: Your answers lean toward a gentle pet you get to know slowly, down at floor level. Plan for a pen with room to move and time together on the floor each day. A rabbit rescue can walk you through what the first week looks like.

results.title: Your Match: Fish
results.description: Your answers lean toward a calm pet that fits a busy schedule and a small space. Plan for a tank, a filter, and a set time each week to check the water. A local fish store can help you choose fish that live well together.

results.title: Your Match: A Bird
results.description: Your answers lean toward a social, talkative pet that likes having people nearby. Plan for a roomy cage in a lived-in room, fresh food each day, and time to talk with it. A bird rescue can help you choose a first bird.
